title: The terrible duet
text: A karaoke machine has appeared. {name} knows the words; neither of us knows the tune.
endings: We found a verse we could manage.
Our duet became a memorable disaster.
Their favourite song got a surprisingly brave performance.
later: They practised that verse again.
They sent me a reminder of our spectacularly wrong note.
They suggested another favourite for next time.

title: An awkward invitation
text: {name} has invited two people who no longer speak to each other.
endings: A seating plan kept the evening workable.
A short visit avoided a long confrontation.

later: They planned seating before another gathering.
They tried another brief meeting.
They checked boundaries before inviting the group again.

title: The impossible recipe

later: They reused our task list for another meal.

title: A competitive afternoon
text: A friendly game with {name} is becoming suspiciously serious.
endings: Clear rules protected the result, though the tension stayed.
Working together changed the mood.

They remembered whose rules we had tried.

title: The unread book
text: {name} has recommended a book. I only got through the first chapter.

endings: A narrow discussion was better than pretending.
We found something else we both wanted to do.
Their favourite passage explained the recommendation.
later: They picked a shorter recommendation next time.
Our new activity became a regular plan.

title: The group photograph
text: {name} wants a photo; somebody dislikes being photographed.

endings: The photo included only willing people.

title: A hobby takeover
text: {name} wants our quiet hobby session to become a public competition.

later: They organised a manageable contest.

They revised the format after our trial.

title: The scenic shortcut
text: {name} knows a “shortcut” that looks longer than the normal walk.

title: A blunt compliment
text: {name} has made something they love. I like parts of it, but not all.

Celebrating the effort left room for pride.
Their request made my feedback easier to give.

They kept making things despite imperfect results.

title: A last-minute cancellation

title: The second-hand find
text: {name} spots a ridiculous object at a second-hand shop and thinks it belongs in our shared joke.
answers: Take a photo and move on
Ask what they would do with it
endings: A photograph preserved the joke without clutter.
We left the object to bewilder another shopper.

They repeated the joke on a later walk.
They drew a mock design for their imaginary collection.

title: The brave introduction
text: {name} is nervous about joining a new local group.

Let them choose how to arrive

A short visit lowered the pressure.

They returned for a longer visit.

title: A tempting vacancy
text: {name} hears about a better role but would need to learn something new.

endings: Requirements made the opportunity more concrete.
A pause separated excitement from pressure.

They finished the first step and reviewed the next.

title: The crowded calendar
text: {name} has said yes to too many plans, including ours.

title: A presentation disaster

title: Two good offers
text: {name} has two opportunities: a secure routine or an uncertain project.

Let them test the uncertain option
endings: Comparing trade-offs exposed what security costs.

title: The housewarming challenge
text: {name} is moving and has vastly underestimated the number of boxes.

They remembered which help had mattered most.

title: The uncomfortable joke
text: {name} makes a joke that lands badly. They are embarrassed rather than defiant.

title: The missing notebook
text: {name} cannot find the notes needed for tomorrow. The group chat is already blaming everyone.

later: They started keeping a shared study list.
They muted the chat before it became another argument.
They asked earlier when they needed a hand.

title: The chat went quiet
text: A short message from {name} reads colder than usual. No one can agree what it meant.
endings: A private question cleared up part of the misunderstanding.

title: Two plans, one evening

title: A room with no shelves

later: They made a plan before another difficult gathering.

title: A letter from years ago
text: {name} finds an old letter from a friend they lost touch with. They are unsure how much to say.

endings: A short note opened the door without promising too much.
